question: Can the existing oracle variance-reference power reduce the finite-solution region relative to ordinary logit when a useful predictor is shrunk toward the true attribute-only choice probability?
model: Same binary Gaussian signal/intercept corrected-logit model as Theorem1. Let mu=expit(gamma*S), g0=P(Y=1|S,Z) for the independent-flip proxy, and g_s=mu+s*(g0-mu). No estimator or tuning rule is introduced.
fixed_dimensional_reference: For one Gaussian orthogonal coefficient, K=E[(mu-g0)^2], Cov(A,B_s)=s*K, Var(B_s)=s^2*K. Existing PPI++ power clips tau/((1+tau)*s) to[0,1]. Compute its actual existence boundary and the ordinary boundary on the same model.
checks: Direct conditional summation verifies the covariance identity and strictly improved fixed-dimensional reference variance at the selected positive power.
At gamma=0 independently evaluate the unit-power scalar formula using normal-tail integration and root finding.
Check 100/200-node quadrature and multiplier gradients; retain any failures without dropping model conditions.
At strength1 recover the existing calibrated-oracle reference power and boundary conventions.
finite_simulation_decision: Choose a mechanism illustration only after the population audit, label that selection explicitly, and retain comparisons with ordinary logit, oracle variance-reference power, and an explicitly fixed smaller positive power on matched draws. No Monte Carlo run has been specified or started in this population plan.
claim_limit: This is a consequence of the existing compensated-boundary theorem and established variance tuning. It is not a new general failure theorem for PPI++,not a new tuning method,and not evidence of uniformly worse point estimates.
